messages:
Sam: Heads-up — we've got a 429 burst hitting about 8% of requests for a handful of orgs in eu-west-1 over the last 2m. Creating a thread to coordinate triage.
Maria: Thanks. Any pattern on specific API keys or routes?
Sam: Mostly text-generation /v1/completions and a couple of long-stream chat sessions. Initial query: 6 org keys account for ~70% of the 429s.
Kevin: Oncall here. Are these real vol spikes or quota enforcement?
Sam: Looks like enforcement + burst queues filling. Rate limiter logs show per-key token bucket rejections after sustained small bursts — comment: burst window seems too tight for some enterprise keys.
observability-bot: alert: quota_exhaustion_spike - 8% 429s over 120s in eu-west-1. threshold=5% (runbook: /runbooks/quota-429-escalation)
Jen: CS flagging — two paying customers reported degraded UX. We may need a templated notification if we escalate.
Maria: Can you paste the PromQL and the dashboard link? Need to add to incident notes.
Sam: Dashboard: https://internal.grafana/redwood/d/abcd123/429-burst-detection
Sam: Query we're using:
```
sum by(org_id) (increase(http_requests_total{status="429",region="eu-west-1"}[2m]))
/ sum by(org_id) (increase(http_requests_total{region="eu-west-1"}[2m]))
```
Maria: ok. Suggest we add a secondary signal for sustained latency and error ratio at route-level so we don't page on short-lived blips.
Kevin: Agreed. Proposed escalation steps: 1) Page oncall at 5% 429s sustained 2m for orgs with >100rps. 2) Auto-create incident in Opsgenie with runbook link. 3) If >10% for 5m, page eng-platform and product.
Jen: Add CS slack pager at >10% so customer ops can start communication.
Sam: For mitigation: we can temporarily increase per-key burst window or bump token refill for the flagged orgs, and enable autoscaling on dedicated pools for that region. Quick mitigation command (internal):
```
# increase burst window for org
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/admin/ratelimit/adjust \
  -d '{"org_id":"ORG123","burst_window_ms":2000,"refill_rate":1.5}'
```
Kevin: We should be cautious with blanket bumping — could hide abusive traffic. Only allow manual increase for verified enterprise keys. Add an approval step in the runbook.
Maria: I'll add the approval checkbox and a short checklist to the runbook. Sam, can you open PR to update runbook markdown? Link to docs: https://confluence.redwood/eng/runbooks/quota-429-escalation
Sam: On it — will add precise thresholds, the PromQL, and the mitigation curl snippet.
observability-bot: note: creating alert rule draft: quota_429_per_org_rate - evaluate_every=30s, for=2m, threshold=0.05
Kevin: Also add an automute for noisy orgs in weekend windows (low priority) — avoids pager fatigue. Put that under ops policy.
Jen: I'll draft a customer broadcast template and attach to the runbook. Keep it short + transparent.
Sam: Assignment: Sam -> update runbook and PR; Maria -> add approval checklist + dashboard panel; Kevin -> update pager/escalation policy in Opsgenie; Jen -> customer template. Review tomorrow 10:30 PT. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: incident created: QC-429-1801234567 (priority: P2) linked to runbook /runbooks/quota-429-escalation
Kevin: Closing loop — once PR is merged let's run a simulator on staging to ensure no false positives.
Sam: Will run simulation after PR. Will post results here.
Jen: Thanks everyone. Keep me posted if CS needs to notify any customers ASAP.
Maria: One more ask — add a per-route fallback policy in the console UX so product teams can set softer throttles for non-critical paths. Ticket created: ENG-9876.
Sam: Good idea. Adding to product backlog.
Kevin: End of thread for now. Monitoring continues.
